agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new breathing, bowel, skin, hormone, heart or nerve symptoms promptly; these may be immune inflammation.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement
Effects may start after the final dose

patient.urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team immediately for new or worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin/eyes, much less urine, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine, or a spreading/blistering rash. For severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or other immediately dangerous symptoms, seek emergency care. Do not wait for the next infusion.
patient.consent_support: Discuss the aim for your exact lung setting, likely benefit, alternatives, important immune risks and how treatment may be paused or stopped. Some side effects need long-term medicines. Ask about fertility, pregnancy, breastfeeding and effects on daily life.
patient.safety_note: Immune effects can happen on any day and after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card and tell any healthcare team that you receive nivolumab.

day_groups.title: Your treatment visit
day_groups.body: The team checks blood results, symptoms and medicines before the prescribed infusion or injection. Tell the nurse immediately about itching, flushing, breathlessness, dizziness or feeling suddenly unwell.

day_groups.title: Between visits
day_groups.body: You may feel well between infusions, but immune inflammation can begin at any time. Keep a short symptom record and take medicines exactly as prescribed. Contact your team about new symptoms instead of waiting for your next appointment.

support.title: Sickness medicines
support.text: Nivolumab alone has minimal sickness risk. Routine preventive anti-sickness medicines or premedication are not usually required; the team may prescribe symptom relief.

support.title: Immune alert card
support.text: Carry your alert card during treatment and afterwards. Show it when seeking urgent care; symptoms can be mistaken for an infection or an ordinary stomach upset.

support.title: Hormones and steroids
support.text: Some immune effects need steroids or hormone replacement. Follow the prescribed plan and do not stop steroids suddenly. Ask for help if symptoms worsen or you cannot take essential medicines.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding requires a specialist decision; contact your team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.intro: Nivolumab can help the immune system control some previously treated lung cancers. Some people benefit for a long time; others do not benefit.
evidence.interpretation: Trial results describe groups, not an individual prognosis.
evidence.population: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
evidence.limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.

rationale.summary: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause the immune system to inflame healthy organs.

factors: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.
ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function.

Hypersensitivity and symptomatic ILD are exclusions. Significant autoimmune disease, symptomatic CNS metastases, active clinically significant infection and systemic steroids >10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent are cautions. Prior checkpoint therapy requires current access review.
alternatives: Other systemic treatment, suitable targeted therapy, clinical trials and supportive care.
limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.
Shared non-lung indications remain in the protocol; this patient/evidence suite is lung-focused.

key_points: No nivolumab dose escalation/reduction; use Table 3 organ-specific hold/stop pathways.
Monotherapy Grade 3 colitis is a hold; Grade 4 is permanent stop.
Grade 2 myocarditis is a hold; Grade 3–4 is permanent stop.
Use CTCAE v4 and assess immune causality; raw labs are not a diagnosis.
Current source contains IV and SC options; cHL IV only.

administration: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.
IV sterile non-pyrogenic low-protein-binding filter 0.2–1.2 micrometres; no push/bolus; 10 mg/mL or dilute to at least 1 mg/mL with sodium chloride 0.9% or glucose 5%.

evidence.population: Pooled n=854, advanced squamous/non-squamous NSCLC after platinum, ECOG ≤1.

endpoints.interpretation: Minimum follow-up 64.2/64.5 months; pooled randomised population, not a personal prognosis or a separate q28/SC efficacy estimate. Database locks: 8 May 2019 (017) and 16 May 2019 (057).

evidence.qualitative_result: Nivolumab can help the immune system control some previously treated lung cancers. Some people benefit for a long time; others do not benefit.
limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.

chapters.intro: Confirm the formulation with your team.

items.title: Administration
items.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV over 60 minutes OR 1200 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 4 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.

items.title: Course length
items.text: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.

items.title: Pauses
items.text: Treatment may be held or stopped for side effects. Nivolumab is not routinely dose-reduced. Tell the team about missed appointments.

chapters.title: Tests and review
chapters.intro: New symptoms matter even when recent tests were normal.

items.title: Before starting
items.text: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests establish a baseline; discuss existing illness and all medicines.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 4-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 4. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

items.title: Response review
items.text: Your team assesses progression before cycle 4; later scans follow the consultant plan.

chapters.title: Practical support
chapters.intro: Tell your team what matters to you.

items.title: Energy and activity
items.text: Balance activity and rest. New marked fatigue with dizziness, headache, thirst or weakness needs assessment.

items.title: Medicines and pregnancy
items.text: Bring all medicine/supplement details. Discuss fertility and breastfeeding. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the final dose.

items.title: Sickness
items.text: Minimal sickness risk: routine preventive sickness medicines are not usually required. Your team may prescribe symptom relief.

chapters.title: When to get help
chapters.intro: Use your oncology urgent contact plan.

items.title: Report promptly
items.text: Report new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe pain, yellow eyes, reduced urine, severe headache, weakness, unusual thirst or a spreading/blistering rash immediately. Use your oncology contact plan; severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or severe chest pain needs emergency care.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Tell the nurse immediately about a reaction during the infusion or injection.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Continue monitoring for at least 5 months after the final dose. Show your immune alert card to anyone treating you.

patient.phases_note: There is no planned chemotherapy induction or maintenance switch in this monotherapy pathway. Treatment is reviewed regularly and may be held, stopped or changed.

rationale.summary: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause the immune system to inflame healthy organs.
rationale.setting: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
factors: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.
ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function.

Hypersensitivity and symptomatic ILD are exclusions. Significant autoimmune disease, symptomatic CNS metastases, active clinically significant infection and systemic steroids >10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent are cautions. Prior checkpoint therapy requires current access review.
alternatives: Other systemic treatment, suitable targeted therapy, clinical trials and supportive care.
limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.
Shared non-lung indications remain in the protocol; this patient/evidence suite is lung-focused.

key_points: No nivolumab dose escalation/reduction; use Table 3 organ-specific hold/stop pathways.
Monotherapy Grade 3 colitis is a hold; Grade 4 is permanent stop.
Grade 2 myocarditis is a hold; Grade 3–4 is permanent stop.
Use CTCAE v4 and assess immune causality; raw labs are not a diagnosis.
Current source contains IV and SC options; cHL IV only.

evidence.population: Pooled n=854, advanced squamous/non-squamous NSCLC after platinum, ECOG ≤1.
evidence.comparison: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2 weeks versus docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV q3 weeks.
evidence.applicability: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.

endpoints.interpretation: Minimum follow-up 64.2/64.5 months; pooled randomised population, not a personal prognosis or a separate q28/SC efficacy estimate. Database locks: 8 May 2019 (017) and 16 May 2019 (057).
Same pooled trial population and comparator; this endpoint is not overall survival.

evidence.qualitative_result: Nivolumab can help the immune system control some previously treated lung cancers. Some people benefit for a long time; others do not benefit.
limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.
After protocol amendment, 23 nivolumab patients switched to 480 mg q4 weeks; this does not provide a separately randomised q4-week efficacy comparison.
evidence.harms: Immune organ inflammation may be serious, fatal, delayed or persistent; hormone replacement may be permanent.
